article.name: GrayMatter
article.summary: GrayMatter is a local-first Go memory store and MCP server for agent facts, with hybrid retrieval, revision/tombstone handling, optional citation and subject-aware tools, and optional knowledge-graph extraction. This review is pinned to current upstream source and does not measure runtime quality or performance.

who_what.text: The official README presents GrayMatter as a persistent memory layer for Go agents, packaged as a local binary that can run as an MCP server or be embedded as a Go library. It describes integrations including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other MCP clients.

architecture.text: The `Fact` record stores agent namespace, text, ULID, creation/access metadata, decaying weight, optional embedding, supersession marker, confidence declaration, kind/pin fields, and lineage projection. Citation evidence and subject projections are hydrated from versioned side stores rather than persisted in the fact row itself.

The store uses bbolt for facts, sessions, metadata, agent namespaces, pending-vector work and related indexes; the default persistent chromem-go index lives under the data directory, while a `VectorStore` interface allows other backends. A reserved `__shared__` agent ID holds shared facts. bbolt serializes concurrent writers with its file lock; the store can fall back to read-only on lock contention unless strict-write behavior is selected.

The README documents a lifecycle of recall, prompt injection, agent writes, then asynchronous consolidation. Current release documentation says consolidation performs maintenance such as decay/pruning and configured graph extraction; generative compaction is disabled. MCP `full` is the default profile, while `core` opts into citations and subject-based writes and adds combined project/shared search behavior.

behavior.text: Writes create facts with a generated ULID and initial weight. The README exposes `remember`, MCP `memory_add`, and Go `Store.Put` paths. In the `core` MCP profile, a write may include a source, literal quote, subject, or replacement target; those fields are opt-in and the legacy `full` profile retains legacy input semantics.

Revisions can atomically add replacement text and tombstone selected source facts in one bbolt transaction. A nonempty `SupersededBy` immediately excludes the old fact from recall while leaving a tombstone available to list/export/TUI; explicit deletion removes a fact record. `Retire` marks selected facts as removed without a replacement. Unpinned tombstones can later decay and be pruned.

Recall fuses vector similarity, keyword relevance and recency using reciprocal-rank fusion; configured default weights are vector 1.0, keyword 1.0, recency 0.5. It returns top-k injectable fact text. The README documents an optional relevance floor, confidence filtering/weighting, aliases for query expansion, and `--explain` ranking receipts. Alias facts are excluded from injectable ranked results.

The integration guide says core search reads project and `__shared__` memory together and can fetch an omitted citation by fact ID. The legacy full profile keeps single-namespace search behavior. The default MCP catalog exposes seven tools; core is an explicit profile choice.

metrics.evidence: The implementation has hybrid top-k retrieval and optional relevance filtering, but this review did not score answer-bearing retrieval or abstention.
Explicit revisions atomically tombstone selected prior facts; no correction sequence or stale-value probe was run.
Retirement excludes facts from recall and explicit deletion can remove a row; no deletion, backup, restore, or leakage probe was run.
Facts are stored by agent namespace and a shared namespace is intentionally readable across agents. No cross-namespace or deployment authorization workload was run.

The optional citation profile stores writer-declared source and quote snapshots tied to fact identity/content; the code calls this evidence untrusted and captured time is receipt time, not verification. No answer was adjudicated against a source.
The README describes upstream benchmark methodology and latency gates, but this review ran no system or benchmark and collected no timings.
The README reports upstream token and inference-cost comparisons; those are source-reported claims only and were not reproduced here. No token, cost, or storage workload was measured for this review.

limits.text: This is a bounded inspection of the official README, integration guide and selected Go implementation files at the verified current head. The system, tests, and benchmarks were not run.

The fact `Confidence` label is the writer's declaration rather than calibrated probability or independent verification. Citation source and quote strings are writer-declared untrusted evidence; captured time records receipt, not verification. These fields do not establish that an answer is supported.

Namespace separation and the `__shared__` convention are code-level storage and retrieval scopes. This review did not test authorization, deployment configuration, filesystem boundaries, or cross-process access control.

The reviewed paths do not establish real-world recall quality, whether users reliably correct or forget facts, whether optional providers are configured securely, or the operational behavior of every custom vector backend.

benchmark.note: No GrayMatter runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Source observations and upstream-reported figures are not results from this project review.
